title: Constant scalar restriction identifies geometric module adjunctions
statement:
Let $(C,J)$ and $(D,K)$ be sites small in one coefficient universe and let $u:\operatorname{Sh}(D)\to\operatorname{Sh}(C)$ be a geometric morphism, with $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ and $u^{-1}$ preserving finite limits [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Fix a commutative ring $B$, constant ring sheaves $R_C=\underline B_C$, $R_D=\underline B_D$ and their constant units $\iota_C,\iota_D$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Supply a ring isomorphism $b:u^{-1}R_C\cong R_D$ whose adjunct $\gamma:R_C\to u_*R_D$ takes constant scalar $a$ to constant scalar $a$; this equality is an equality of maps from the constant presheaf. Write $u_R^*\dashv u_{*,R}$ for the ringed module adjunction along $b$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction], and $u_B^*\dashv u_{*,B}$ for the induced geometric adjunction on sheaves of fixed-$B$ modules. Let $C_C,C_D$ be the actual constant-scalar restriction functors [def-sfb-constant-ring-module-restriction], with their inverse equivalences given by extending local scalar actions. There are natural isomorphisms
$$C_Cu_{*,R}\cong u_{*,B}C_D,\qquad C_Du_R^*\cong u_B^*C_C.$$
The first is the identity on the common underlying additive direct-image sheaf. The second is its adjunction mate: after the displayed comparisons both Hom adjunction bijections, units and counits agree. For an open localization $j$ of these topoi, suppose the ringed and fixed-$B$ open pullbacks have their specified left adjoints $j_{!,R}$ and $j_{!,B}$. There is a natural isomorphism $C_Cj_{!,R}\cong j_{!,B}C_D$ compatible with these adjunctions, including their units and counits. This includes restriction to every localized site [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]; no hypothesis on points, coefficients being finite, or an underlying scheme is made.

source.place: Tag 00YV, proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi, case (6) and compatibility of adjunctions; agent-written constant-ring/fixed-scalar comparison serving original steps 8 and 11.

proof.text: For a $B$-scalar $a$, let $a_C:1\to R_C$ and $a_D:1\to R_D$ be its constant sections, and let $\lambda_a^N:N\to N$ be multiplication by $a_D$. The normalization hypothesis on $\gamma$ says $\gamma a_C=u_*(a_D)$, with the canonical terminal-object identification understood. By the definition of the induced ringed direct image, its action restricted to $a$ is therefore $u_*(\lambda_a^N)$: insert $\gamma a_C$ in the scalar input of $u_*$ of the action of $N$. This is exactly the scalar endomorphism defining the fixed-$B$ direct image. Addition and underlying sheaves already agree. Thus the identity of $u_*N$ is a $B$-linear isomorphism $\beta_N:C_Cu_{*,R}N\to u_{*,B}C_DN$. Both functors send a module map to the same underlying additive map, so these identities are natural.

source.place: Tag 00YV, proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi, case (6), fixed-ring actions by endomorphisms; agent-written comparison with ringed module actions.

proof.text:
Write $E_C,E_D$ for the inverse equivalences of the statement, which extend the fixed-$B$ action along $\iota$ to the unique constant-ring action on the same underlying abelian sheaf; by [lem-cbc-constant-ring-module-sheaves] these are quasi-inverse equivalences to $C_C,C_D$ on every site, with no nonzero-ring or nonempty-site hypothesis, so the equivalences are proved rather than assumed. Their evaluation isomorphisms $E_CC_C\cong1$, $C_CE_C\cong1$, and their $D$ analogues retain every underlying additive map. In particular restriction gives bijections on Hom sets, not merely injections. Put $P=u_B^*$ and $Q=u_{*,B}$, and put $\widetilde L=C_Du_R^*E_C$. For arbitrary fixed-$B$ module sheaves $A,H$, the supplied equivalences, the ringed module adjunction, and step 1 give natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}_B(\widetilde L A,H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{R_D}(u_R^*E_CA,E_DH)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{R_C}(E_CA,u_{*,R}E_DH)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_B(A,QH).$$
In the last bijection apply $C_C$, then $\beta_{E_DH}$, then $Q(C_DE_DH\cong H)$. Thus this explicitly defines an adjunction $\widetilde L\dashv Q$. Its units and counits are the images of identity arrows under these bijections and their inverses.

source.place: Tag 00YV, proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi, case (6), fixed-ring actions by endomorphisms; agent-written comparison with ringed module actions.

proof.text:
Apply the unit-compatible uniqueness lemma to $\widetilde L\dashv Q$ and the specified $P\dashv Q$, with the identity comparison of their common right adjoint. It gives a natural isomorphism $\widetilde L\cong P$. Evaluate it at $A=C_CM$ and use the supplied evaluation $E_CC_CM\cong M$ to obtain $\alpha_M:C_Du_R^*M\cong PC_CM$. More explicitly, writing $\eta_R,\eta_B$ for the specified units, the uniqueness equation is
$$Q(\alpha_M)\circ\beta_{u_R^*M}\circ C_C(\eta_{R,M})=\eta_{B,C_CM}.$$
This specifies the comparison for the given adjunctions, so it is the adjunction mate of $\beta$, rather than an independently chosen isomorphism of pullbacks.

source.place: Tag 0B65, lemma-transformation-between-functors-and-adjoints; agent-written application of the unit-compatible uniqueness of left adjoints.

proof.text:
Let $\Phi_R,\Phi_B$ denote the Hom adjunction bijections. For $f:u_R^*M\to N$, expand $\Phi$ as right adjoint applied to the arrow followed by the unit. Naturality of $\beta$ and the unit equation of step 3 give
$$\Phi_B\bigl(C_D(f)\circ\alpha_M^{-1}\bigr)=\beta_N\circ C_C\bigl(\Phi_R(f)\bigr).$$
This is agreement of the Hom bijections. For the counit take $M=u_{*,R}N$ and $f=\varepsilon_{R,N}$; its ringed adjunct is the identity. The fixed-$B$ adjunct of $\varepsilon_{B,C_DN}\circ P(\beta_N)$ is $\beta_N$, so injectivity of $\Phi_B$ gives
$$C_D(\varepsilon_{R,N})=\varepsilon_{B,C_DN}\circ P(\beta_N)\circ\alpha_{u_{*,R}N}.$$
Together with the already displayed unit equation this proves both requested compatibilities.

source.place: Tag 0B65, lemma-transformation-between-functors-and-adjoints; agent-written application of the unit-compatible uniqueness of left adjoints.

proof.text:
For the specified open localization $j$, use its pullback comparison $\alpha^j:C_Dj_R^*\cong j_B^*C_C$ from steps 1--4. For a fixed-$B$ sheaf $H$ on the localized topos and $A$ on the ambient topos, the given open adjunctions and equivalences give
$$\operatorname{Hom}_B(C_Cj_{!,R}E_DH,A)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{R_C}(j_{!,R}E_DH,E_CA)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{R_D}(E_DH,j_R^*E_CA)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_B(H,j_B^*A).$$
The last bijection applies restriction, $\alpha^j_{E_CA}$, and $j_B^*(C_CE_CA\cong A)$. Therefore $C_Cj_{!,R}E_D\dashv j_B^*$. Apply the same unit-compatible uniqueness lemma to this adjunction and the specified $j_{!,B}\dashv j_B^*$, and then evaluate at $H=C_DN$. This gives $\kappa_N:C_Cj_{!,R}N\cong j_{!,B}C_DN$. If $\Psi_R,\Psi_B$ are the open Hom bijections, its defining equation, extended from units by naturality, is
$$\Psi_B\bigl(C_C(f)\circ\kappa_N^{-1}\bigr)=\alpha^j_M\circ C_D\bigl(\Psi_R(f)\bigr),\qquad f:j_{!,R}N\to M.$$
This equation holds because $\kappa$ is the unit-compatible comparison: for $g:j_{!,B}C_DN\to C_CM$ one has $\Psi_B(g)=j_B^*(g)\circ\eta^{j}_{B}=\widehat\Psi(g\circ\kappa_N)$, where $\widehat\Psi$ is the Hom chain just displayed, and $\widehat\Psi(C_C(f))=\alpha^j_M\circ C_D(\Psi_R(f))$ by its construction. For the units take $M=j_{!,R}N$ and $f=\mathrm{id}$: $\Psi_B(\kappa_N^{-1})=\alpha^j_{j_{!,R}N}\circ C_D(\eta^j_{R,N})$, the agreement of the open units. For the counits take $N=j_R^*M$ and $f=\varepsilon^j_{R,M}$, whose ringed adjunct is the identity: the displayed equation gives $\Psi_B(C_C(\varepsilon^j_{R,M})\circ\kappa^{-1}_{j_R^*M})=\alpha^j_M$, while $\Psi_B(\varepsilon^j_{B,C_CM}\circ j_{!,B}(\alpha^j_M))=j_B^*(\varepsilon^j_B)\circ\eta^j_{B,j_B^*C_CM}\circ\alpha^j_M=\alpha^j_M$ by naturality of the unit and the triangle identity. Injectivity of $\Psi_B$ gives $C_C(\varepsilon^j_{R,M})=\varepsilon^j_{B,C_CM}\circ j_{!,B}(\alpha^j_M)\circ\kappa_{j_R^*M}$, the agreement of the open counits.

proof.text: For the localization $\mathcal C/U$, restriction evaluates on $(V\to U)$ as evaluation on $V$. The ring of the localized site is $R_C|_U$; by [lem-weil-pbc-site-constant-restriction] (with $M=B$) the constant sheaf $\underline B_{\mathcal C/U}$ is canonically $R_C|_U$, and its sheafification unit at $V/U$ is the restriction of $\iota_C$, i.e. $\iota_{V/U}(a)=\iota_V(a)$. This identification is multiplicative, since both units are ring maps and are locally surjective. So $C_{\mathcal C/U}$ is the constant-scalar restriction of [def-sfb-constant-ring-module-restriction] for this ring. Consequently restricting the constant action $\iota_V(a)m$ before or after $C_C$ is the same action and the same map on each section. This gives the pullback comparison for localization directly, also after relocalization. The open-left-adjoint argument of step 5 only used this pullback comparison and the specified left adjoints, so applies to localized sites whenever those adjoints are supplied, without needing the localization to be open. None of the arguments uses points, a scheme, a finite coefficient ring, a nonzero coefficient ring, or a terminal object in the presented site.
